shared.surfBiteReport: The most current report available for the Panama City Beach and 30A surf zone is approximately 3 weeks old (mid-July 2026), so treat this as recent but not this week's conditions. With water at 84°F, baitfish are thick along the beaches from Dune Allen through PCB and predators are stacked behind them — the pattern holding across this entire stretch. Spanish mackerel, whiting, and redfish have been the primary surf-zone species, with jack crevalle mixing in; focus your casts on the deeper cuts and troughs between sandbars rather than bombing long casts past the second bar, as most of these fish are feeding much closer to shore than anglers expect. The bite windows are tight in peak summer heat — dawn through roughly 9 a.m. and again the last two hours before sunset are producing the most action, with midday fishing slow unless you drop into deeper troughs or shade your presentation. Sand fleas, shrimp, Fishbites, and Fish Gum are the go-to surf baits; keep a fast spoon or gotcha plug rigged on a second rod for the Spanish mackerel schools that appear and disappear quickly along the beach. Pompano are present but numbers are typically thinner on this coast in peak August heat compared to spring, as they tend to push to slightly deeper, cooler water once surface temps climb above the low 80s.
